question: 2 years ago, the value of my car was ₹3,62,500. If the value depreciates by 2% every year, then now its value (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A depreciation of 2% means the new value becomes 98% (or 49/50) of the previous year's value.

Present Value = Initial Value × Multiplying Factor²

⇒ Present Value = 362500 × (49 / 50) × (49 / 50)

⇒ Present Value = 145 × 2401 = 348145

**∴ The correct answer is ₹348145.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Value of the car 2 years ago (P) = ₹3,62,500

Rate of depreciation (R) = 2% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Present Value = P × (1 − R / 100)T

**Calculation:**

⇒ Present Value = 362500 × (1 − 2 / 100)²

⇒ Present Value = 362500 × (98 / 100)²

⇒ Present Value = 362500 × (49 / 50) × (49 / 50)

⇒ Present Value = 362500 × 2401 / 2500

⇒ Present Value = 145 × 2401

⇒ Present Value = 348145

**∴ The correct answer is ₹348145.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Depreciation Formula

When the value of an asset decreases uniformly by R% every year, the final value after T years is found using A = P × (1 − R/100)T.

Successive Percentage Change

The effective net change of two successive percentage changes a% and b% is given by [a + b + (a × b) / 100]%. For two 2% depreciations, the net change is −2 − 2 + (4/100) = −3.96%.

Population Growth

If a value (like a town's population) increases at R% per annum, the new amount after T years follows the standard compound interest formula: A = P × (1 + R/100)T.
